name: application-side-menu
title: Side Menu
description: Persistent sidebar navigation panels for dashboards and application shells, featuring logo, nav links, sub-menus, and user profile areas.
useWhen: The application has multiple top-level sections and needs persistent visible navigation.
Building a dashboard or admin panel shell where the sidebar stays in view across all pages.
Navigation requires expandable sub-sections or nested menu items that would clutter a top nav.
avoidWhen: Screen space is at a premium on a primary mobile experience — use a bottom tab bar or hamburger drawer instead.
The site has only three to five top-level pages — a top navigation bar is simpler.
The sidebar content would be mostly empty on most pages — surface navigation only where it adds value.
responsiveBehavior: Side menus collapse to a hidden off-canvas drawer on small viewports, triggered by a hamburger button. On medium screens and above, the sidebar appears persistently.
accessibility: Wrap the sidebar in a <nav> element with aria-label='Main navigation' to identify it as the primary navigation landmark.
The currently active page link should carry aria-current='page'.
Expandable sub-menus use native <details>/<summary> for keyboard-accessible disclosure without JavaScript.

variants.title: Logo, links with accordion menu and profile details
variants.description: Full-height sidebar with a logo at top, expandable accordion nav sections in the middle, and a user profile row at the bottom.
accessibility: Native <details>/<summary> handles accordion sections; active link uses aria-current='page'; avatar has meaningful alt text.

variants.title: Logo, links with accordion menu and profile details (Dark)
variants.description: Full-height accordion sidebar with logo and user profile adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Dark nav link and active-state colors must meet WCAG AA contrast requirements.

variants.title: Icon, links with tooltips and logout action
variants.description: Compact icon-only sidebar where each nav item shows a tooltip with its label on hover, with a logout button at the bottom.
accessibility: Icon-only nav items must have visible tooltips and aria-label attributes for screen reader users.

variants.title: Icon, links with tooltips and logout action (Dark)
variants.description: Compact icon-only sidebar with tooltips and logout adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Icon colors and tooltip text must meet contrast requirements on dark sidebar backgrounds.
